procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism (factory must be outside a free zone, have a MoIAT industrial licence and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Apply for the Certificate of Origin for India through the Ministry of Foreign Trade e-service: log in, complete the form, upload proof of factory registration and commercial invoice, pay the fee online, submit, and print the approved certificate.
Pay the certificate fee: AED 50 (estimated for invoice value up to AED 100000).
Ship the goods directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading or storage.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed.
Keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.
The certificate is valid for 12 months from issue, covers one import, and should be issued before, at or within five working days of export.
An issued certificate can be amended once for a fee of AED 20; the invoice amount and destination cannot be changed.

caveats.note: The CEPA lowers the duty on this line but does not remove it.
The '+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Factory declared in a free zone: likely not eligible for the ministry's factory registration; confirm with the ministry.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022).
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.

Factory registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added. The 40% value-added letter is a registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
Minor typing or formatting errors are tolerated on the certificate; discrepancies in signature or seal are not.
India's certificate form governs entry into India; the agreement says box 8 but India's form says box 9.
